subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Group 18
hotspots.description: This glowing column at the far right of the table is Group 18 — the noble gases. All six members sit stacked here.
hotspots.positionHint: The highlighted far-right column of tiles below the balloon.
hotspots.function: Shows where the noble gases live on the periodic table.

hotspots.label: Full outer shell
hotspots.description: The small atom model shows a completely full outer shell — every electron space filled. This full shell is why noble gases never need to react.
hotspots.positionHint: The small atom model floating beside the balloon, visible when the shell-view layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the full outer shell that makes noble gases stable.

hotspots.label: Noble gases in daily life
hotspots.description: The balloon is filled with helium and the tube glows with neon — two famous uses of the calm noble gases.
hotspots.positionHint: The balloon on the left and the neon tube beside it.
hotspots.function: Shows the everyday objects made from noble gases.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A helium balloon and a neon tube float centered above a table section, lit with soft neutral studio light — the neon tube may carry a gentle warm glow ONLY when the reaction-test layer demonstrates it, handled by the app; the mesh itself has no emissive. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the balloon is a muted pastel coral, the tube a soft warm-amber at rest, the table tiles paper-white. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (molecular green / amber / slate accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Balloon: muted pastel coral, matte, roughness ~0.5. Neon tube: warm translucent amber at rest (alpha ~0.6), roughness ~0.4. Table tiles: paper-white, roughness ~0.55. Atom model: small teal electrons on a translucent hairline ring. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow (neon lighting up) is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: the noble gases shown through their calm, everyday uses, built to be read as 'the full-shell family that never reacts.' Four procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: two objects floating at center height — (a) a helium balloon (a simple ellipsoid ~0.8 wide, muted pastel coral, matte, with a thin string falling from it) and (b) a bent neon-tube shape (a thin torus segment, ~0.9 long, warm translucent amber at rest).

2) SHELL VIEW (toggleable layer): a small atom model floats beside the balloon — one translucent hairline ring with tiny teal electron spheres completely filling it (e.g. 8 electrons for neon, or 2 for helium), showing the full outer shell.

3) REACTION TEST (toggleable layer): a tiny spark (a small soft amber dot) appears near the gas tube; the app plays a short 'nothing happens' beat — the gas stays calm, nothing reacts. The tube may glow briefly here (app-driven).

4) GROUP 18 ON TABLE (toggleable layer): below, a flat section of periodic table (paper-white tiles, ~9 x 5). The entire far-right column is given a faint muted green cast and slight raise — Group 18.

Camera: framed so the balloon and tube are large and centered with the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: HeliumBalloon, String, NeonTube, ShellAtom, ShellElectrons, ReactionSpark, TableSlab, Group18Column. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
